Our approach

Personalised care. Informed choices. Individualised planning.

Every person considering breast enhancement has different anatomy, breast tissue, aesthetic preferences and expectations. At QuantumHealth, our approach begins by understanding those factors before we discuss any available option.

We aim to make complex treatment choices easier to understand by presenting the potential benefits, limitations, recovery considerations and risks of each approach — so you can make decisions grounded in accurate information rather than promotion.

Whether you are exploring breast augmentation surgery, fat transfer or a non-surgical treatment, our focus is on transparent information and a carefully considered treatment plan.

Treatment pathways

Explore your options by category

Two broad pathways, each with different intended outcomes, evidence and risks.

Injectables · regenerative · skin quality

Non-surgical options

Selected injectable, regenerative and skin-quality approaches, considered with attention to evidence, suitability and approved indications. Not every non-surgical treatment is shown to increase breast volume.

Learn more

Implants · autologous fat transfer

Surgical options

Understand breast implants, silicone gel-filled implants and autologous fat transfer, including recovery and long-term considerations.

Learn more

An important clinical distinction

Injectable fillers, threads, PRP and biostimulators should not be presented as interchangeable alternatives to breast augmentation surgery. Their evidence, indications and ability to increase breast volume differ substantially, and a procedure being described as “non-surgical” does not by itself make it safe.

Meet Dr. Vikas Singh

Dr. Vikas Singh is a cosmetic dermatologist, hair transplant surgeon and regenerative medicine practitioner, with more than 20 years across cosmetology, dermatology, hair transplantation, anti-ageing and regenerative medicine.

His stated philosophy centres on healthspan — bringing appearance, regeneration and longevity into one considered plan for each patient.

How your consultation works

A clear, five-step pathway

A consultation is a conversation, not a commitment. Progression to treatment only happens if it is clinically appropriate for you.

01

Tell us what matters to you

Share your concerns, preferences, medical history and the outcomes you hope to achieve.

02

Clinical assessment

Your clinician reviews relevant medical factors and determines whether further examination, imaging or specialist assessment is appropriate.

03

Understand your options

Review suitable procedures, alternatives, expected limitations, recovery considerations and potential risks.

04

Make an informed decision

Proceed only if the selected treatment is clinically appropriate and you have had time to understand and consent to it.

05

Follow-up and aftercare

Receive procedure-specific instructions, follow-up arrangements and guidance on when to seek medical attention.
